subject: humanities
passage: In much Baroque music, the keyboard player's part was written as a single bass line with small numerals beneath it indicating which chords to play. How those chords were spaced, ornamented, and rhythmically distributed was left to the performer, who was expected to vary them from one performance to the next. Modern editions that print a fully written-out keyboard part are therefore convenient but potentially misleading: they make one editor's choices look ______, when the composer had in fact expected each player to fill in the harmony differently.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The word "when" sets up a contrast between how the printed part looks and what the composer intended. The composer expected each player to fill in the harmony "differently," so the problem with a printed part is that it makes one version look like the only correct one.
explanation.A: Correct. "Definitive" means final and authoritative, which is the misleading impression a printed part gives when the composer expected many versions.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Arbitrary" means chosen without reason. A printed part does not make choices look random; if anything, it makes them look official.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Anachronistic" means belonging to the wrong period. The text's contrast is between one fixed version and many possible versions, not between old and modern styles.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A part that is fully written out looks fixed, not improvised; improvising is what the composer expected the players to do.
